messages.message: ### Step 2: Direct Translation Translate each source line into Bulgarian, guided by the Reference Translation and Step 1 analysis. Output: ONE Bulgarian line per source line (preserve line count and end punctuation). Rules: - Follow the meaning from Reference Translation. - For "so X that Y": keep resultative structure, do NOT convert to "because". - No internal punctuation; copy only end punctuation from source.
Тя ми наложи толкова тежест със страха който излезе от нейния поглед, че аз изгубих надеждата от височината.

### Step 3: Word Table & Coverage Check Build a word table from Step 2 translation, mapping each source word to its target equivalent. Output: ONE Markdown table (all lines combined). Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Word/Phrase] | [Back-Translation] | [Status: OK/MISSING/WRONG/GRAMMAR/UNNECESSARY] Mark GRAMMAR for agreement errors (gender, number, case) or other grammatical mistakes. Mark UNNECESSARY for elements present in source but not needed in target language (e.g., articles that target language omits naturally). After the table, list any MISSING, WRONG, GRAMMAR, or UNNECESSARY items.

**Word‑by‑Word Mapping Table**
| Source Word | Contextual Definition | Target Word / Phrase | Back‑Translation (EN) | Status | |-------------|-----------------------|----------------------|-----------------------|--------| | **questa** | demonstrative pronoun, subject – “she” (female agent) | **Тя** | she | OK | | **mi** | clitic dative – “to me”, experiencer | **ми** | to me | OK | | **porse** | verb “caused, imposed” | **наложи** | imposed / caused | OK | | **tanto** | adverb of quantity – “so much” | **толкова** | so much | OK | | **di** | preposition linking “gravezza” – “of” (not needed in BG) | — | — | UNNECESSARY | | **gravezza** | noun “heaviness” (affective state) | **тежест** | heaviness | OK | | **con** | preposition “with” (introducing accompanying circumstance) | **със** | with | OK | | **la** | definite article – “the” (feminine) (not needed in BG) | — | — | UNNECESSARY | | **paura** | noun “fear” (the emotion that arises) | **страха** | the fear | **GRAMMAR** (incorrect gender/definite form; should be *страхът*) | | **ch'uscia** | relative clause “that came out / emerged” | **който излезе** | that emerged | OK | | **di** | preposition “from” (source of fear) | **от** | from | OK | | **sua** | possessive adjective “her” | **нейния** | her | OK | | **vista** | noun “sight” (visual perception) | **поглед** | sight | OK | | **ch'io** | relative pronoun + subject “that I” | **че аз** | that I | OK | | **perdei** | verb “lost” (first‑person past) | **изгубих** | lost | OK | | **la** | definite article – “the” (not needed in BG) | — | — | UNNECESSARY | | **speranza** | noun “hope” (the mental expectation) | **надеждата** | the hope | OK | | **de** | preposition “of” (linking hope to its content) | **от** | of / from | OK | | **l'altezza** | noun “the height” (metaphorical lofty goal) | **височината** | the height | OK |

### Items Requiring Attention - **GRAMMAR:** *paura* → **страха** (incorrect gender/definite article; correct form is **страхът**). - **UNNECESSARY:** All Italian articles/prepositions that have no direct counterpart in Bulgarian: **di** (line 52), **la** (line 53), **la** (line 54).
All other source words are adequately rendered in the Bulgarian translation.

### Step 4: Correction & Final Output Fix any MISSING, WRONG, or GRAMMAR items from Step 3. Reorder within line if needed; do not add new content words. (or "none") - Corrected: ... (or "no change") Output final Bulgarian text in ONE code block, line by line (no extra prose).
